Spotlight: Reliable 6yo who was a close second in the Chester Cup (2m2f, good; 3lb higher today) on reappearance under Toby Moore; not so good in the Queen Alexandra at Royal Ascot (2m5f, good to firm) but he did stay on into a fairly remote fourth; strong each-way candidate.

OwnerName: A Cope, B Roberts And J Biggane
Spotlight: Eight AW wins, two last winter in 2m handicaps; however, he has tons to prove on turf record (0-6) and even best AW form does not look good enough.

Lightly raced 4yo; proved that he does indeed possess serious stamina when upped from 1m6f to 2m4f at Royal Ascot (good to firm) last time, bang there almost throughout in first-time blinkers and beaten a head; back up 4lb but has a big shout.

Signed off last term with a win at Haydock (1m6f, good) on the only time he's worn cheekpieces; overcame trouble at Hamilton (1m5f) on reappearance and although it was hard work when he plugged on from the rear to be sixth of 16 at Royal Ascot (1m6f, good to firm; 9-4 favourite) it was his best performance on the figures and gave encouragement for 2m+; cheekpieces return.

OwnerName: Berkshire Parts & Panels Ltd No1 Fanclub
Spotlight: Cheekpieces enlisted for last three starts, winning on first occasion and good sixth in the Chester Cup (2m2f, good); 16-1 for Queen Alexandra at Royal Ascot (2m5f) six weeks ago but weakened right out of it in the last half-mile; that was his first race on firmer than good since start of career three years ago, so there's a big question mark about the ground.

4-22 in France, including two 2m wins; changed hands and left Andre Fabre before having a crack at a Royal Ascot handicap (2m4f, good to firm) in which he came from well off the pace to be fifth of 20; that good effort (off 1lb lower than today) puts him in the picture.

Held up and stays 2m4f; a superb 2024 culminated in his Cesarewitch win at Newmarket off the same mark as today; 2025 campaign went from promising to frustrating (including with trouble in running) to disappointing; however, his fifth of 20 to Believitanducan in Northumberland Vase at Newcastle five weeks ago was a step back in the right direction.

Runner-up in 2024 on his only start on good to firm; won at up to almost 2m5f as hurdler; back to Flat with two wins on good ground (Ascot and Chester) and another on AW at Newcastle, last named the 20-runner Northumberland Vase in which he clearly held the upper hand through the final 2f; up another 5lb with a different trip, ground and track, but has to be shortlisted.

Below form on the Flat this year, for instance 11th to Believitanducan in the Northumberland Vase last month; not proven beyond 2m in this sphere but he switched back to hurdles for a 2m6f win at Stratford 12 days ago, which might give some renewed hope.

The lack of any win since a maiden hurdle in January 2024 (first run for Willie Mullins) is a concern but he's produced solid efforts on Flat over 2m2f, 1m6f and 2m on his last three starts and may well be an out-and-out stayer; no shock if he's on the premises.

Seven-race maiden, with four seconds including at Doncaster (1m4f; odds-on) and Pontefract (2m1f; made most in first-time cheekpieces) on his two starts this season; reverts to just a tongue-tie and relatively unexposed as a stayer but others have to be more persuasive.

Not proven on firmer than good; two wins followed by two Goodwood places on his only four appearances over 2m for Emma Lavelle; first run for new connections was voided before the race warmed up; has a competitive mark and possibilities going beyond 2m, but this is also a better race.

OwnerName: J R B Williams & Emdells Limited
Spotlight: Latest Flat start was his first win, by 7l in a four-runner race at Pontefract (2m1f, good to firm) last August for Ollie Sangster; seven races over hurdles for new connections, winning two (2m5f/2m3f) of the last three; probably has a good mark, so needs a second look, but this is a step up in class.

All British Flat wins (five of them) have been at Goodwood but the last four were on soft ground, latest in June 2025; sixth in this race in 2023 and fifth last year, both on soft; last August saw his only run on good to firm in the last three years and he wasn't discredited, but he needs to step up on this year's efforts, particularly as he's 4lb out of the handicap.

14th at 100-1 in this race in 2024; won at Kempton this year over hurdles and on AW Flat, and similar Flat form over that 2m on last two runs, but much better is needed from 5lb out of the handicap today; 7lb claimer is called up.

Running away with a 2m2f race on heavy going under 7lb claimer at Nottingham last October was a clear career best at the time; virtually matched that form in three of his races in a mixed campaign this year and maybe an increased stamina test will help, but being 5lb out of the handicap won't.

A year between her debut for Charlie Johnston and her comeback for this yard, and absent for seven months since; came in for good support at Southwell in January, though, when pulling too hard; worth a market check again.
Big price for her Windsor debut recently, when finishing last after fluffing the start; will need a big step forward.

Yard enjoyed a good month and this filly about sets the standard, having come away with an interesting newcomer at Southwell last Thursday; nothing wrong with her previous Ffos Las third either and she's respected in first-time headgear.

250,000gns yearling who's a half-sister to Listed winner Brunch (twice successful on Tapeta) and useful handicapper Golden Voice (1-1 on Tapeta); looks to have been found the ideal race on her belated debut.
Half-sister to five-time turf winner Sunny Corner, who improved once handicapping (as did her dam, also for Stuart Kittow); no surprise to see her follow suit.

Debut Chester fifth well advertised since; looked to find the drop to 5.7f against her (stamina on the dam's side) last time following an awkward start and she's one to bear in mind; maybe in handicaps after today, though.
22,000euros yearling who's a half-sister to four winners; the market will show what's expected on debut but it wouldn't surprise were she to need some time.
Three solid efforts this summer, latterly when not quite seeing out 1m on her handicap/turf debut a fortnight ago; one to consider back on the AW and back down in trip.
Trainer saddled four big-priced winners on the spin early in the week; this filly would be the biggest shock of all, having finished well held in two turf runs.

Easy to back and finished well held on her 6f debut here last November; would want to see good support from the outside stall under 7lb claimer Molly Keegan-Price (0-7 to date) before including her in calculations.

RaceName: Kids Eat For £1 At The Border Minstrel This Summer Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Took this race last year and landed a handicap at Southwell (1m3f, Tapeta) in March; well beaten over 1m here last Saturday and,  although this trip should suit him better, he needs to put that performance behind him; blinkers return.

RaceName: Kids Eat For £1 At The Border Minstrel This Summer Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Three of her four wins have come here, including one over this trip; landed a similar event at Wolverhampton (9.5f, Tapeta) in March and not hard to forgive her performance at Pontefract (1m4f, good to firm) a fortnight ago; high on list back in distance.

RaceName: Kids Eat For £1 At The Border Minstrel This Summer Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Landed a gamble in a similar contest at Wolverhampton (8.6f, Tapeta) in March last year, but moderate since including on her first start since wind surgery at Redcar (1m1f, good to firm) 12 days ago; blinkers given a go this time; worth monitoring in the market.

RaceName: Kids Eat For £1 At The Border Minstrel This Summer Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Both wins came in turf handicaps around this time last year (1m2f/1m4f); has run with credit lately including when fourth of 13 in a 0-60 handicap over C&D five weeks ago; one of the likelier winners.

RaceName: Kids Eat For £1 At The Border Minstrel This Summer Classified Stakes
OwnerName: N J Dalgarno & W R Ellis
Spotlight: Third of 13 in a similar contest over C&D last month and only just lost out when third of ten at Ayr (1m, good) on his penultimate outing; record of 0-28 is hard to ignore, though.

RaceName: Kids Eat For £1 At The Border Minstrel This Summer Classified Stakes
Spotlight: 0-8, but has run well to finish fourth in both starts since returning for this yard after a 20-month absence; still unexposed and not dismissed up in trip.

RaceName: Kids Eat For £1 At The Border Minstrel This Summer Classified Stakes
OwnerName: Maj Green, S Croft & S Whitaker
Spotlight: Out of the frame in three starts on turf since returning in May, but drops to this level for the first time since winning at Ripon (1m2f, good) just under a year ago; can't be ruled out.

RaceName: Kids Eat For £1 At The Border Minstrel This Summer Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Made a successful reappearance in a similar contest over C&D in March; placed only once in five in handicaps since, but respected back in this company.

RaceName: Kids Eat For £1 At The Border Minstrel This Summer Classified Stakes
Spotlight: 0-7; showed a little ability last autumn and drops to this level for the first time, but heavy defeats in both starts since returning in April leave her with enough to prove; cheekpieces given a go.

RaceName: Kids Eat For £1 At The Border Minstrel This Summer Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Well held in five starts over 6f-8.5f; drops in grade but others are still more compelling.

Ended his 2yo campaign with AW Listed win and has proved consistent this term, most recently best of the near-side runners in the Jersey at Royal Ascot; holds solid claims in another change of headgear, albeit is comfortably held by Talk Of New York on Heron Stakes running.

Campaigned mostly at 7f; had wind/gelding operations prior to easily justifying favouritism in Goodwood handicap; second best (behind Andab) in the near-side group in the Jersey Stakes since; the only course winner in this field and there are 1m/1m1f scorers on the dam's side of his pedigree.

Useful colt whose 2yo form featured a success in AW Group 3 and fourth in the Middle Park, both over 6f; proved resurgent in 7f Listed contest at Chester most recently, making the frame; however, has something to find on ratings upped further in distance.

Ran below expectations when a warm order for the Jersey at Royal Ascot (2-2 previously) but bounced back with a creditable effort against his elders in 7f Group 3 at York a week later, while leaving the impression he'll be suited by this step up to 1m combined with first-time headgear; remains of interest, with further progress still plausible.

Showed a strike-rate of 3-4 as a 2yo; has gradually found his form this season and recorded a clearcut success in Newmarket Listed event (1m, good to firm) most recently, hitting the line strongly and building on his second-place finish in the German 2,000 Guineas; back in the zone and may rate higher still; one of the main contenders.

Progressive colt whose record is 3-5; came off strong pace set by a stablemate and stormed clear to win the Heron Stakes at Sandown on penultimate start, then ran well in the St James's Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot (1m, good to firm) despite pulling hard in the early stages; the form pick and his chance will be cemented if settling better than last time.

Had wind surgery prior to reappearance win and now goes in first-time tongue-tie having dropped right away in the Heron Stakes; short of the standard set by Talk Of New York in this rematch but has the same strike-rate (3-5) as that rival and, with the Sandown run perhaps best excused, it's too soon to suggest he can't resume improvement.

Operating below last year's peak form but posted sound effort when third at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) last week and remains on same mark as for emphatic C&D success in November; no surprise if he features.

Unable to land a telling blow on first two stable starts but rewarded good market support when scoring by a neck at Southwell (7f) this month and remains well handicapped on older form; high on the list.
Didn't see out 8.6f when sixth here this month but finished close up off today's mark on consecutive 7f Polytrack starts in the spring and has possibilities on this drop back in trip.

OwnerName: Hot To Trot Racing And R Mitchell
Spotlight: Unexposed 3yo who displayed clear promise in all three qualifying races, most recently when fifth of 12 in 1m Kempton maiden in April; drops back in trip for handicap debut; open to improvement.

OwnerName: I Foster, D Fish, W Dale & S Dale
Spotlight: Made low-key seasonal/handicap debut when 13th of 19 at Ascot (6f, good) in May but had wind surgery during subsequent 12-week break and is dropped in grade for this AW debut; moves up in trip; could still have significant potential.

Placed twice over 6f for new stable this spring (turf/Polytrack) and also has form over 7f; needs to bounce back from a poor turf run in first-time cheekpieces two weeks ago but has slipped to a tempting mark and will be dangerous if he responds well to first-time blinkers.
Dual 7f Polytrack winner last summer; well below best this year but at least her recent fifth of eight at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm) was a step back in the right direction.

Dominated from the front at Kempton (7f; wore cheekpieces) in March, his second handicap, but dropped out disappointingly on both outings last month (8.6f/7.3f); has a point to prove in first-time blinkers, and his tendency to race too freely remains a worry.

Won C&D maiden in March, her second start, but largely disappointing since; raced too freely when midfield in 8.6f handicap here this month; drops back to 7f with hood fitted today; needs to get career back on track.
Six-race maiden; made quite promising seasonal debut when fifth of 12 at Kempton (7f) last month but her turf run two weeks ago was underwhelming; others have more pressing claims.
Eight-race maiden; made a low-key stable debut in April (6f) and was pulled up (lame) on turf the following month; back up in trip here; not the most obvious answer.

RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Sent off at 4-6 when scoring by 4l on debut at Yarmouth (6f, good to firm; second has done well since); not well drawn when well beaten in the Coventry; gelded since; related to dirt/AW winners; contender.

RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 140,000gns yearling by Blue Point; 33-1 when well beaten in a conditions race at Beverley on debut (5f, good to firm); down in grade on AW debut.

RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 160,000euros breeze-up buy; by Minzaal; half-brother to a Group-placed 5f winner out of a 6f winner; interesting newcomer from powerful yard.

RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: By Dark Angel; 170,000euros breeze-up buy; second foal of a 6f/7f winner; worth a market check on debut.

RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: 325,000gns yearling by Night Of Thunder; fifth foal; brother to one winner (7f) and half-brother to two more; dam a Listed 5f winner; interesting on debut.

RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 45,000gns yearling; well-beaten last of eight when a 40-1 shot on York debut in May (6f, good); needs to improve.

RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Home-bred by Ardad; half-brother to a 6f winner; likely to be better for the experience.

RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Well beaten on her two starts so far; looks one for nurseries.

Blew his chance at the start in most recent handicap attempt but generally consistent otherwise in the last year and ties in with several of today's rivals on Royal Hunt Cup form; 2-2 at Goodwood and looks interesting back here despite remaining on a career-high mark.

Contrasting performances since fitted with hood, winning readily at Meydan but disappointing favourite in the Royal Hunt Cup returned to British soil; something to prove off an unchanged mark, which remains 10lb above the last one he raced off prior to UAE stint.

Currently in a consistent vein of form that ties him in with some of today's opponents; creditable third to Indalo at Sandown most recently; Goodwood record comprises a couple of second-place finishes at this meeting, including in this race last year; solid claims.

Record of 2-4 since being gelded features a success at Epsom on Oaks day when overcoming trouble; down the field in the Royal Hunt Cup 12 days later but perhaps the race came too soon; rested over six weeks since and may rebound.

Completed a Meydan double early this year; came up short in the Royal Ascot handicap he'd won in 2024 but ran respectably, behind an unbeaten rival, at Hamilton most recently; has to overcome the widest draw returned to a bigger stage.

Progressive; unlucky second in the 2025 Cambridgeshire and fared best of the far-side runners in this year's Royal Hunt Cup; justified favouritism in the Coral Challenge at Sandown (1m, good to firm) and is 2lb well in under a small penalty for that deserved change of luck; respected.

Very consistent on AW since last turf appearance; respectable seventh, despite enduring a nightmare passage, in this contest two years ago but is 5lb higher and lacks recent match practice in this compensation attempt; absent since March.

Prevailed by a neck from Indalo at Newbury in May but has been unable to confirm the placings in the Royal Hunt Cup and Coral Challenge; current mark is stiffer than the one off which he finished sixth, amid traffic issues, in this race two years ago.

Ex-French 5yo whose form figures of 0080 in Britain reflect that he's not a solid option; did well to finish eighth in the Royal Hunt Cup, having started slowly, but folded tamely in the Coral Challenge last time; best watched unless the market speaks positively.

OwnerName: Sir M Arbib,B Arbib,C Budgett & A Kheir
Spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo who looked a smart prospect early doors and whose disappointing runs are perhaps best forgiven in hindsight; had wind surgery prior to a resurgence, leading his group for a very long way, in the Royal Hunt Cup (handicap debut); interesting assuming he builds on that effort.

Reached a useful standard in France; well supported for handicap attempts at Royal Ascot in 2025 (hindered by traffic issues) and 2026 (stable debut; creditable fourth over 7f) since racing in Britain; may well build on the reappearance effort and show progress; one to consider.

Commenced last season with wins in the Lincoln and useful AW handicap; not in the same form since, latterly posting two duck eggs this term for new yard, latest in the Royal Hunt Cup when behind several of today's opponents; major revival is required.

Record of 2-4 features a clearcut win from the front in valuable prize at Gowran Park, showing marked improvement; returns to a more suitable trip/grade after trailing home last in the Irish Derby, and interestingly his yard landed this race with 3yos in 2013 and 2019; one to bear in mind.

Comes with a degree of risk as he's often slowly away and needs the cards to drop right; however, form this term includes placed efforts in two major handicaps, while Goodwood record comprises a creditable sixth in this race 12 months ago and success next time; this may be the day to catch him, with renowned hold-up wizard Jamie Spencer up for first time.

Ran encouragingly in a couple of races won by English Oak during his spell in Meydan and wasn't disgraced at Goodwood (7f) on Wednesday; however, still has a poor strike-rate as it's two years since his sole success; steps back up in trip/class.

Landed the Chesterfield Cup at this meeting in 2023, initiating a notable double; however, has failed to score since and current mark reflects a broad decline in his form; drop to Class 3 had no effect last time and he looks a shadow of his former self.

Registered one of his 2025 wins at Goodwood, off current mark to boot; however, broadly out of sorts this term and needs to stage a revival; creditable fourth in this race in 2023 and 2024 but was in better form both times.

Has a record of 3-4 at Pontefract and 1-1 at Ascot; 0-16 elsewhere and his form since last success doesn't augur particularly well for this big assignment; failed to beat a rival when dropped back in grade latest start; first attempt at Goodwood.

RaceName: Call 01902 390016 To Name A Race Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Dual winner in France (turf, Polytrack) who's struggled in three runs for this yard having been picked up for 32,000euros early in the year; this more realistic, dropping from Listed company, but would want to see some support before considering her.

RaceName: Call 01902 390016 To Name A Race Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Pulled hard all three starts, latest when running away with a C&D maiden a fortnight ago (well held in 1m races on turf previously); remains unexposed but she'll find this somewhat tougher now handicapping at a decent level.

RaceName: Call 01902 390016 To Name A Race Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Couple of absences since winning a 6f handicap here last spring off a 2lb higher mark; the return to Tapeta is an obvious plus point but she's very hit and miss, and will need to improve somewhat on this season's two efforts after two months off.

RaceName: Call 01902 390016 To Name A Race Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Drawn wide on her Chester comeback before over-racing back in the hood over a stiff 7f last time; stable been enjoying a purple patch of late and she's one to consider back on the AW.

RaceName: Call 01902 390016 To Name A Race Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Made all when winning her novice on Polytrack last autumn (race produced winners); well held in two runs at Meydan in the winter, latterly in Listed company, but still has some potential at this level for her much in-form yard.

RaceName: Call 01902 390016 To Name A Race Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Likes it here; came back to form last Wednesday at Lingfield (turf) but has little room for manoeuvre off this mark, albeit she'll be 1lb higher from the weekend; vulnerable to improvers.

RaceName: Call 01902 390016 To Name A Race Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Having a first run on Tapeta since winning her maiden at Southwell last autumn; the impression remains that she's capable of better and it will be interesting to see how she goes in the market back from a short break.

RaceName: Call 01902 390016 To Name A Race Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: 1m AW winner in France late last year, since when she's unseated at the start and not seen it out in one run over hurdles; another non-completion for her new yard a fortnight ago, when pulled up at Newmarket.

RaceName: Call 01902 390016 To Name A Race Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Dual Tapeta winner for Ollie Pears last autumn before a fruitless spell in Dubai for her current yard; much better at Southwell six weeks ago, back from a break, and today's extra furlong will help; goes on the shortlist.
Showed some promise last season, including on the AW; got off the mark when neck-winner of a 1m6f handicap at Nottingham last time (good to firm; 20-1); up 3lb; a possible.
Convincing 1m4f winner here in January; best run since when a clear second at Hamilton last time (1m5f, good to firm); now tries 2m for the first time; chance.

Placed at Hamilton (1m3f) in May and over 1m4f here (first-time cheekpieces) in June; didn't shape like an obvious stayer when 5.25l fifth of eight at Ayr last time (1m7f, soft), but worth another chance over this trip back on AW.
Winner at Ayr (1m5f) and Musselburgh (1m4f) in June and ran another sound race when neck second at Carlisle last time (1m3f);  fair efforts on previous tries at 2m; one to consider.

OwnerName: A Whillans, C Spark, J Wright
Spotlight: Only win came over C&D last August when rated 1lb lower; below form both runs this season but should do better having had wind surgery.
Two Lingfield AW wins (1m4f) and a handicap hurdle win (2m4f) for Ben Pauling; some fair runs without winning for this yard but not at his best after 406-day absence this season.

Dual winner on the AW in France (1m, 9.5f); mainly disappointing for new yard, although fair third of five in first-time visor at Beverley two runs ago (1m4f, good to firm); on a fair mark, but beaten more than 8l on two tries at this trip.
Maiden; two fair efforts on the AW towards the end of last year, including a C&D third, but not so good since.
Unexposed filly who has finished well beaten in three bumpers and in three novice events on the AW (1m4f); no improvement in cheekpieces (on again) last time; handicap debut.

Returned this year having been gelded and he's been an improved model, winning the Group 3 Palace House at Newmarket (5f, good to firm) and the Group 2 Temple Stakes at Haydock (5f, good to soft) before leading home those who raced in the centre group when tenth of 26 overall at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm); usually front-runs and this speedy track should suit him better than Ascot (ran well in this last year); strong claims despite 3lb penalty.

Won the Group 1 King Charles III Stakes at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm) last June then missed the rest of the season; mixed form this year but he showed spark when second to Night Raider at Haydock in May and today's expected frenetic gallop will be right up his street; not ruled out.

5yo front-runner who has been better than ever this year, comfortably winning a handicap at York (5f, good) in May and posting a fine fifth of 26 at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm) last month; third in Group 2 Sapphire Stakes at the Curragh (5f, good to firm) recently and he could build on those last two efforts, which were on stiff tracks, now on a downhill course; respected.

OwnerName: MPS Racing Ltd & The Ayrshire Tradesmen
Spotlight: Won a handicap at this meeting in 2023 and he won this race last year (good to soft; seems versatile ground-wise); he hasn't been at the very top of his game this year but there have been encouraging signs on his last two starts and he could play a leading role back at Glorious Goodwood.

Trained in Sweden, where he has posted comfortable wins in 6f Listed races on his last three starts; faces a higher calibre of opponent today and he was soundly beaten in a dirt Group 3 at Meydan in February, but he might not be a forlorn hope each-way in view of his more recent exploits.

6yo who has been campaigned over further for the majority of his career but he's been a progressive sprinter this season, finishing third in a Group 3 at Sandown (5f, good) on July 4 then runner-up in Group 2 at the Curragh (5f, good to firm) last time; however, this tougher race demands more.

Reappeared with good second to Night Raider in the Group 3 Palace House at Newmarket (5f, good to firm) and bounced back from below-par run at Royal Ascot to win at Sandown (5f, good) four weeks ago, taking that Group 3 for the second year in a row; has won here and is firmly in calculations.

Three Group 1 wins, the latest last October, and second in this race in 2024 (seventh last year); step back in right direction when close seventh at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm) but finished last at Sandown subsequently (slowly away) and it's been an underwhelming campaign; has to raise her game.

Respectable effort in midfield in the Group 1 King Charles III Stakes at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm) last month before 1l fifth of 13 in Listed race at York (5f, good to firm); however, a career best is needed today.

OwnerName: D Bevan And Mrs D Bevan
Spotlight: Won the Group 1 Commonwealth Cup at Royal Ascot (6f, good to firm) last June before fine third in this race under a penalty (good to soft); however, she's struggled to hit the same heights subsequently.

Third in the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf Sprint last October and he's gone close in a couple of Listed races at York (5f, good to firm) this season, the latest three weeks ago in first-time cheekpieces (retained); however, his form has to go to a new level if he's to win this.

He's the sole Ballydoyle runner and was second in the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf Sprint last October; however, unable to match that form this season and was behind Partisan Hero and Jakajaro at the Curragh last time.

OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Third in the Group 3 Molecomb over C&D (good) last July and reappeared with 3yo Listed win at York (5f, good) in May; not beaten far when seventh of 13 in Listed race at York (5f, good to firm) three weeks ago and still lightly raced, but he's down the pecking order on ratings in this line-up.
Runner-up in the Group 3 Molecomb (5f, good) over C&D 12 months ago and returned to form with Listed win at Ayr (5f, soft) last month; however, it's likely she'll come up short now back up in grade.

C&D and Listed winner in last season's 2yo campaign, and she ran a mighty race when going close at 50-1 in the Group 1 Commonwealth Cup at Royal Ascot (6f, good) last month; failed to back that up in Group 3 at York three weeks ago but not ruled out in view of her peak performance.

RaceName: Thank You, Jane Broad, For All Your Support Handicap
OwnerName: Duaij Al Khalifa & Ahmad Al Qassimi
Spotlight: Proven competitive since handicapping, backing up her Southwell second with a solid turf debut last time (rather drawn away from the action); she's been upped 3lb, though, so will need to find a bit more if she's to break her duck.

RaceName: Thank You, Jane Broad, For All Your Support Handicap
Spotlight: Found an ordinary maiden (7.2f) when off the mark here in the spring and has been held in two handicaps since; struck into at Windsor, though, before slowly away and hitting traffic behind Lightning Glory and Little Margot last time; stable form a big plus.

RaceName: Thank You, Jane Broad, For All Your Support Handicap
Spotlight: Made all when winning an ordinary fillies' handicap on turf early last month; ran to a similar level off her revised mark last time, again from the front, when behind Lightning Glory at Southwell; no obvious reason she won't go well once more.

RaceName: Thank You, Jane Broad, For All Your Support Handicap
Spotlight: Three AW efforts better than his five turf runs, latterly when comfortably beating a subsequent winner over C&D early in the month; a 6lb rise demands more but he may well be up to it.

RaceName: Thank You, Jane Broad, For All Your Support Handicap
Spotlight: Inclined to over-race in three runs, including two in the hood, and she'll have to settle better from a wide stall going back up in trip; has shown a fair level of ability in maiden/novice company but needs more on her AW debut.

RaceName: Thank You, Jane Broad, For All Your Support Handicap
Spotlight: Pulled hard a couple of times, including in the hood, and will have to settle better now going beyond 7f for the first time; however, backed up his Musselburgh win off his revised mark last time, when awkwardly away, and has improvement left in him.

RaceName: Thank You, Jane Broad, For All Your Support Handicap
Spotlight: Expensive to follow in maiden/novice company in the winter before gelded; didn't look to quite see out 9.5f here on his second run back a month ago and he's one to consider.

RaceName: Thank You, Jane Broad, For All Your Support Handicap
Spotlight: Pulled hard on her comeback and bettered that when a clear second to an improver at Bath seven weeks ago; nudged up 2lb for that and this is stronger but she holds each-way claims.

RaceName: Thank You, Jane Broad, For All Your Support Handicap
Spotlight: String of poor efforts at huge prices this season; expect more of the same.

RaceName: Thank You, Jane Broad, For All Your Support Handicap
Spotlight: Half-brother to the yard's useful sprinter Star Of Mehmas and has only run in sprints to date, regressing since returning from wind surgery last winter; it all hinges on the new trip and first-time headgear.

OwnerName: Middleham Park Racing D Turner B Roberts
Spotlight: Has done well since going handicapping, winning at Chelmsford (6f) and Yarmouth (5f) in the spring before good seconds at Nottingham (5f) and Wolverhampton (6f); not quite so good last time; stiff 5f should suit; each-way chance.
Can pull hard; three places but no wins from 11 starts; capable of going well, as he showed when second in two races in the spring (one on the AW) but not particularly consistent.

OwnerName: J Raybould N Skinner D Jenkins
Spotlight: C&D winner in first-time visor in May; well beaten on turf since; course record is 4321; chance back here.
Winner over 6f here in December; best runs since have been here, including neck second to Houndhill over C&D in May; a possible.
Three good runs in AW handicaps in the spring, following close second over 5f here by winning at Wolverhampton (6f); returns after an 84-day break having been gelded.
Close third on handicap debut at Nottingham last October (5f, soft); beaten more than 9l only AW start; bit to prove after below-par reappearance run in June.
Good third of five in a C&D maiden in March (10-11); had a wind op after a poor run at Southwell the following month; mixed form since.
Won a six-runner C&D handicap early last month on only run at 5f; well beaten stepped back up to 6f on turf next time; could go well.
Ex-Ed Walker; close second in two 6f handicaps on first two runs for Harriet Bethell; 2l last of five at Catterick last time (6f); drop in trip could suit; contender.
Bought for 7,000gns out of Harry Charlton's yard in April having shown promise in three AW runs at 5f/6f in January/February; lacks a recent run but quite interesting on handicap debut.
Won a Redcar nursery on handicap debut last October (5f, good); disappointing since, including two runs over this C&D; others preferred.
Has run well on last two starts here, winning over 6f in April and finishing a close second to Dontwasteamoment (now 5lb worse off) when dropped down to 5f here last month; could go well.

RaceName: Regent Seven Seas Cruises Bentinck Conditions Stakes
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Won the Cambridgeshire at Newmarket (1m1f, good to firm) last September and added a Listed win here (1m2f, good) in May, narrowly beating Naqeeb; this front-runner has remained in good form and can make a bold bid.

RaceName: Regent Seven Seas Cruises Bentinck Conditions Stakes
Spotlight: Won the Group 2 Celebration Mile here (good to firm) last August and bagged Listed win at Ascot (1m, good to firm) in May; below par in Group 1 and Group 2 races on last two runs and entitled to respect back down in grade.

RaceName: Regent Seven Seas Cruises Bentinck Conditions Stakes
Spotlight: Well beaten on reappearance in Group 3 at the Curragh (1m2f, good) last month but may have needed that run and he was highly progressive in 1m2f/1m handicaps last season, a campaign that culminated with a win in the Balmoral at Ascot (good); retains potential and not ruled out.

RaceName: Regent Seven Seas Cruises Bentinck Conditions Stakes
Spotlight: Listed winner at Longchamp (7f, good to soft) last May, then beaten on his next eight starts before winning five-runner handicap at Hamilton (8.3f, good) last month; today's task is tougher and he may be vulnerable.

RaceName: Regent Seven Seas Cruises Bentinck Conditions Stakes
Spotlight: Won two handicaps in a row at Meydan (1m1f/9.5f, good) in February before Group 2 second there (1m1f, good); returned from break with good third in the Listed Wolferton Stakes at Royal Ascot (1m2f, good to firm); flopped at Sandown four weeks ago but very much of interest on his earlier form.

RaceName: Regent Seven Seas Cruises Bentinck Conditions Stakes
Spotlight: Runner-up in the Derby in 2024 but nothing like the same force now; after a stint over hurdles he was comfortably beaten in a handicap at Royal Ascot last month; hard to fancy.

RaceName: Regent Seven Seas Cruises Bentinck Conditions Stakes
OwnerName: Barry Taylor/T G Fitzgerald/Prof Paul H Redmond/Barry Fowler
Spotlight: Group 3 winner at the Curragh (1m2f, good) last April and went close under a penalty in the Wolferton Stakes at Royal Ascot (1m2f, good to firm) in June; returned to form in that same Listed race last month, when fourth of 16 (good to firm; Dividend third), and he could have a part to play.

RaceName: Regent Seven Seas Cruises Bentinck Conditions Stakes
Spotlight: Below-par results this season but he may have needed his reappearance run here and got no run in the Wolferton at Royal Ascot (eased), having won that same Listed contest last year (good to firm); won the Group 2 Vintage Stakes here in his 2yo campaign in 2023; major player if at his best.

RaceName: Race & Rest - Wolverhampton Holiday Inn Handicap
Spotlight: Both wins have came on AW over 1m2f at Lingfield this year, latest in April; inconsistent last four starts, respectable fourth here (9.4f) latest; second once in March over 1m3f and this is his first crack at 1m4f.

RaceName: Race & Rest - Wolverhampton Holiday Inn Handicap
Spotlight: Sole win in AW maiden as 3yo, from 20 races; there's plenty of evidence that he can be on the premises, though, including his third here in January on a rare run at 1m4f.

RaceName: Race & Rest - Wolverhampton Holiday Inn Handicap
Spotlight: Short-priced favourite for his two handicaps, coming up short on first occasion (after six months off) but no mistake in 14-runner race at Southwell (1m3f, Tapeta) four days ago; 6lb penalty now but he had something in the tank and is almost certainly well handicapped in this bid for a quick double.

RaceName: Race & Rest - Wolverhampton Holiday Inn Handicap
Spotlight: With her third trainer, first run for him when 40-1 and well beaten at Kempton (2m, AW) this month; overall scores are 0-8 on Flat and 0-5 over hurdles, and clearly her best Flat effort was over 2m1f last September in a first-time visor; 6lb lower today but others are still preferred.

RaceName: Race & Rest - Wolverhampton Holiday Inn Handicap
Spotlight: Won at Worcester (good) on debut last September in the first of his two bumpers; down the field at big odds at Southwell (1m3f/1m4f, AW) and Haydock (11.6f, soft) in his first three races under Flat rules; lacks solid form claims but he has a modest mark for handicap debut.

RaceName: Race & Rest - Wolverhampton Holiday Inn Handicap
Spotlight: Never dangerous from the rear over 1m2f in two starts at Newbury (good) and one at Salisbury (soft); gelded since; scopey sort who is bred for 1m4f and some ability is there, as shown most clearly on second start, so he could be about to come into his own in handicaps.

RaceName: Race & Rest - Wolverhampton Holiday Inn Handicap
Spotlight: Showed promise on good to firm on reappearance, before last month's soft-ground wins at Lingfield (1m1f) and Ayr (1m2f); he had no answers, however, when fifth of 14 to Roc De Fer at Southwell (1m3f, AW) four days ago.
Landed a 6f novice here just under a year ago; held in three starts since beaten a short head at Carlisle (7f, soft) in May, but now 3lb lower and drops in a Class 6 for the first time; shortlisted.
Sole success came in a 6f handicap here last November and he's now 1lb lower, but there's a suspicion that shorter trips suit him best.

Out of an Italian Oaks winner and showed some ability for Harry Charlton last autumn, but three starts since returning for this yard in April have yielded little; best watched unless the market suggests otherwise.
All three wins have come over 7f on Tapeta including one here; just 1lb higher than when successful at Southwell in December and very much respected back on this surface.
Sole win in 21 starts came narrowly over 1m here in March; held since, but is now 1lb lower so a case can be made.
All three wins have come over 6f including one here; not very consistent, though, and a suspicion that this trip stretches him.
Placed three times in six starts for Richard Hannon including when second of 14 at Lingfield (7f, Polytrack) last October, but modest in five outings for this yard and now 0-11; others preferred.

OwnerName: Ms C Dolan & Ms Sarah Harrison-Lamb
Spotlight: Third of five in a muddling event on her debut over C&D last November, but well held in both starts since; more needed now switched to a handicap.
Was having his first start since wind surgery when winning over 1m here in March, but the wheels have come off completely since; best watched for now.
Huge prices all three starts and hasn't finished within 10l of the winner, but there have been glimpses of ability; market interesting on handicap debut.

Stayed on well to win in a good time at York's Dante meeting in May (6f, good) and plenty of scrimmaging meant he didn't get the chance to show what he could do when dropped back to 5f in the Group 2 Norfolk at Royal Ascot (good to firm); interesting that he was a late withdrawal from the Group 2 July Stakes and retains an entry at that level; returns to 6f for his first nursery and one to consider.

Won his maiden on fast ground over 5f at Leicester; finished fifth of 24 runners in the Super Sprint but it wasn't the hottest renewal of that sales race and he had no excuses from a good position; off this mark others hold greater appeal.

350,000gns yearling who was odds-on when a 3l winner on debut at Redcar (7f, good); failed to fire in the Chesham at Royal Ascot (7f, good to firm) but didn't have the ideal track position and it wouldn't be reckless to put a line through that run; looks sharp enough for 6f, over which he holds an entry in the Group 2 Mill Reef.

Home-bred colt from a fine sprinting family; a beaten favourite on debut at Newmarket's Guineas meeting; has got closer in his subsequent races, finishing right behind Clash Of Hearts at Beverley (5f, good to firm) and his Chester conqueror had the form that entitled him to favouritism (6f, good); the potential is there to raise his game on nursery debut.

Third and first (5.7f/5f, firm) on his two visits to Bath before coming up well short when 100-1 for the Norfolk at Royal Ascot; goes this far for the first time but he doesn't look obviously well handicapped.

Confined to 5f since running over 6f on Ascot debut; won a small-field maiden here (good) but came up short in a three-runner nursery at Windsor (good to firm) despite having the run of things up front; he did rally late on, suggesting 6f could be more his trip, but his yard may have better chances.

Half-brother to a 6f 2yo Group 3 winner; finished third of 15 (subsequently promoted to second) in a York novice (6f, good) won by Persian Spring (who now has to concede him 4lb) and has built on that, notably in winning by 5l at Pontefract (6f, good) 40 days ago (made all at odds-on); going the right way and one to be interested in.

OwnerName: Future Champions Racing Syn & Ben Haslam
Spotlight: Ryan Moore won on his only previous ride for Ben Haslam, and this colt won comfortably at Hamilton last time (5f, good to soft); that wasn't a strong race with the runner-up now 0-6 and it's worth noting that he was taken out of a York engagement last month on account of good to firm ground (was due to step up to 6f); however, the Moore link heightens interest for sure.

Progressive colt who had a break of two months after winning his maiden (5f, good) and he beat a consistent rival with the pair clear in a 6f nursery at Nottingham (good to firm); an 8lb rise demands more in this deeper race and stall 1 might not be ideal.

Gelded after second start; held up when far too good for his rivals in a Class 5 novice at Chepstow (6f, good to firm) but raced up with the pace when a fader on handicap debut at York; that was underwhelming but perhaps he'll seek more cover this time.

Unbeaten since gelded, with 6f wins on good to firm at Nottingham (maiden) and Ripon four days ago (nursery); that recent win was never in much doubt having travelled strongly and, although penalised accordingly, the iron is hot; respected.

All runs over 6f; hasn't kicked on from his winning debut (good) but those heavy defeats came in the Woodcote/Windsor Castle and he's been gelded since Royal Ascot where he wore blinkers (now removed); hard to totally discount for last year's winning yard in case he has turned over a new leaf.

Promising efforts before getting off the mark on her fourth start in a novice at Carlisle (5f, good; proven at 6f) two months ago; nursery newcomer and encouraging that she's progressed her RPRs with each run.

Dug deep to edge home in a Newbury novice (6f, good to firm) and probably performed at least as well when a close third on nursery debut at Windsor (11-2); she was given every chance that day and therefore looks vulnerable off an untouched mark.

His most competitive run was on debut and he's been worryingly modest in his last two races, latterly bringing up the rear on nursery debut at York (6f, good to firm; 10-1); not easily warmed to on the back of that effort.
Has performed to a similar level in his first three races, dropped back to 5f last time at Sandown (good); cheekpieces now go on but he makes his nursery debut in a deep race and has to improve.

All runs over 5f; she made all to win her maiden at Beverley on good to soft (beating May Bee In Profit) before trailing home last in the same track's Hilary Needler (good to firm); again showed plenty of early speed that day so questionable whether she wants this extra furlong.

Improved for the cheekpieces at Newbury (6f, good to firm) when beating all bar a well-backed newcomer; whether that form is good enough to defy this mark is debatable but she lurks off a feather weight.
Nearly won off 2lb higher at Kempton three runs back but hasn't threatened since; behind American Style here the last time.
Dual turf winner who was making his AW debut when a rallying third here recently, beaten only a neck; thereabouts.

On a losing run but was only beaten 4l last time at Southwell (5f) in a race won by Naana's Sparkle who was second at Goodwood on Tuesday; hasn't had many chances over this longer trip and he has been running on at the minimum.
Only 3lb higher than for January's C&D win and has continued to run well; 6f specialist with a solid chance, despite stall 10.
Third over C&D on Boxing Day when bidding for a five-timer at this track; still on a competitive mark and her quiet last run was on turf after a break of 158 days; better can be expected back here.
Last season he won three turf handicaps (5f); a dual winner on the AW and it wasn't too shoddy a run at York last week after 53 days off; 2lb above last winning mark.
6f novice winner on turf and also runner-up in a nursery off 3lb higher; hasn't beaten a rival this season but the ability is there should a first-time hood trigger something.
Positively ridden when going close over 6f at Southwell before a disappointing run upped to 7f on turf (soft); not clearly well treated for this handicap debut but may yet do better.
Did well to defy a high draw here two weeks ago, winning well; that took his form figures over C&D to 211; raised 7lb but this 3yo could deal with that.
Won a weak maiden here in November but it's been a very quiet start in handicaps, kept to 6f; has dropped 5lb but reservations for now.

RaceName: James's Gate Irish EBF Median Auction Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Disappointed when well backed ahead of debut at the Curragh (6f, good); more like it upped to 1m at Bellewstown on latest, beaten 5.5l into second; 7f could suit on the evidence of that run and has a nice draw here; place claims.

RaceName: James's Gate Irish EBF Median Auction Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Excellent run on debut at the Curragh (6f, good) when 0.5l behind useful yardstick Immortal Guard; out of depth in 6f Group 3 back there on latest but could do better dropped in class and the step up to 7f could suit (full brother won over 1m).

RaceName: James's Gate Irish EBF Median Auction Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Gary Devlin & C G Bryson & Kevin Osborne
Spotlight: Kameko gelding; 30,000gns foal; brother to Italian 5.5f winner Berkshire Kameo, half-brother to 6f winner Startled Lady (RPR 70); dam unraced sister to 1m/8.5f winner Sir Antonino, out of 6f 2yo Listed winner; respected source and worth a market check on debut.

RaceName: James's Gate Irish EBF Median Auction Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: In the mix in all three starts at 6f-7.5f; beaten 0.5l when third of 13 in a Down Royal maiden (7f, soft) on latest; gelded since and cheekpieces now go on; needs to find a bit more to get his head in front.

RaceName: James's Gate Irish EBF Median Auction Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Space Traveller colt; price rose from E5,000 to E30,000 as a yearling; half-brother to winners Ravenglass (7f-8.6f inc AW; RPR 78) and Grey Sparkle (6f/7f inc 2yo/AW/Germany; 63); dam unraced sister to 5f 2yo Listed winner Delizia, out of half-sister to King's Stand winner Dominica; market best guide on debut.

RaceName: James's Gate Irish EBF Median Auction Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: No impression on debut at Down Royal when 28-1 (7f, soft); similar story upped to 1m at Bellewstown (good) on latest; handicaps beckon after this.

RaceName: James's Gate Irish EBF Median Auction Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Equiano gelding; half-brother to winners Lady Bin (Italian 1m2f/11.5f), Spanish Colt (Spanish 1m/1m1f) and Invincible Fairy (Polish 1m); dam unraced half-sister to 7f-1m1f Group 3 winner Sandiva and Danish 1m1f Listed winner Wentworth; tough task from wide draw on debut.

RaceName: James's Gate Irish EBF Median Auction Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Rated 80 after four outings; runner up twice, on debut at the Curragh (6f, soft) when 6l behind Great Barrier Reef and at Listowel (6.5f, good) in May when 3l behind The Scallionator; not disgraced when beaten 8l in the Windsor Castle on latest; should go well in first time cheekpieces.

RaceName: James's Gate Irish EBF Median Auction Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Mohammed Bin Hamad Khalifa Al Attiyah
Spotlight: Tasleet colt; 25,000gns 2yo; half-brother to three winners inc Bur Dubai (12.3f GB/12.4f Australia; RPR 100) and Emirates Empire (1m4f/1m6f AW; 93); dam 9.4f-1m2f winner (inc AW; 74), closely related to 7f 2yo Listed winner Be Ready; likely best watched on debut.

RaceName: James's Gate Irish EBF Median Auction Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Sent off at 4-1 on debut at Bellewstown (1m, good) but could only manage a 6.25l fourth; will need to improve plenty on that to make his presence felt here.

RaceName: James's Gate Irish EBF Median Auction Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Calyx filly; half-sister to Polish 7f 2yo/1m2f winner Fa Mulan; dam unplaced 7f/1m (RPR 30), half-sister to winners Grande Marques (5f Listed), Bubbles On Ice (useful 1m/8.5f inc 2yo/US), Equity Swap (1m2f) and Optimism And Hope (1m Ire 2yo/US); yard won this with a 50-1 newcomer in 2024.

RaceName: James's Gate Irish EBF Median Auction Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Lucky Vega filly; dam runner-up 7f turf in Japan, half-sister to useful winners Memorial Day (1m-1m4f) and Mutafawwig (6f-1m), out of 1m2f Listed winning half-sister to French Derby winner Anabaa Blue; likely type on paper, well drawn and worth monitoring in the market.

RaceName: James's Gate Irish EBF Median Auction Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Slowly away but showed a bit of ability when a 4.25l fifth of 9 on debut at Cork when sent off at 11-2; bred to appreciate this longer trip but will need to take a big step forward to win this.

RaceName: James's Gate Irish EBF Median Auction Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Sent off at 66-1 on debut at Roscommon (7.5f, good) but shaped with promise, staying on nicely in the closing stages for a 6l fifth behind subsequent Listed winner Dancing Destiny; should improve for that initial experience but drawn very wide here.
0-9 and starting to look exposed, but she represents a powerful yard and the drop in trip may be no bad thing; hood returns.
Not a frequent winner (3-36) but running well on turf lately and has been placed in his last four visits here; one for the shortlist.
Not beaten far into fifth of 13 in a better race at Southwell (7f, Tapeta) eight days ago and remains 2lb lower than when winning this race last year; interesting.
Ex-Sir Mark Prescott; better effort when fourth of eight (just behind Travis) at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) 13 days ago; frame possibilities if building on that in first-time cheekpieces.
0-10 and form has an uneven look to it, but he's off the same mark as when beaten under a length at Ayr (1m, soft) on his penultimate start; a possible for the frame with a repeat.
Veteran who proved he still had what it takes when making virtually all at Southwell in April and is back off the same mark; has won three times over this C&D and no surprise were he to run well.
All three wins came over 7f/1m here last year, the latest from 3lb lower; has a bit to prove now back with his former trainer (who owns him) after six months off; market may be revealing.
0-9; twice runner-up in six starts for Peter Chapple-Hyam, but can't be recommended on his three efforts for this yard; off four months.
1-22, the win coming in a three-runner Chepstow maiden (5f, good to soft) for Nigel Tinkler in August 2024; well beaten in two starts since returning for this yard in May; little appeal.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Often front-runner; four wins over about 1m this year and twice runner-up (Epsom and Chester) in quick succession when stepped up to 1m2f in June; kept on well under usual rider Rose Dawes last time and this trip is unlikely to be an issue, but further improvement is needed for sure.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Returned to form to win at York (1m2f, good) in May and good second of three at Salisbury (1m4f, good to firm) in June; top 1m2f handicap at York three weeks ago proved much too tough and he needs to resume progress.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Tongue tied first time and improved when comfortably off the mark in a novice at Chepstow (1m2f, good to firm) in May, leading over 2f out; handicap debut was a tough task at Royal Ascot (1m2f; 20-1) and he tailed off having led 7f; dropped 2lb and early days.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
OwnerName: Lord N P V J Rothschild
Spotlight: Knuckled down well to assert at Salisbury (1m2f, good) and had a simple task at Yarmouth (11.4f, good to firm) in another novice later in May; put firmly in her place in a 1m4f French Listed race six weeks ago, recording her best rating nevertheless; more is needed on this handicap debut but the best has probably not yet been seen of her.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Found his stride a little too late when pipped on handicap debut at Sandown (1m2f, good) in April; the winner was Lost Boys who's won two major 1m2f handicaps since, latterly at Royal Ascot, but this one's appearance at that meeting (1m4f, good to firm; 4-1) was a backward step when he was slowly into stride and only briefly threatened to emerge from mid-division; now tries 1m3f in headgear first time and these are early days; could bounce back.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 1m4f didn't help when creditable seventh at Royal Ascot; runner-up in all his other five races this season, which could be construed as hard luck but blinkers now replace the recent cheekpieces after his defeat in a Yarmouth maiden last time; others have more pressing claims.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Upped to 1m2f when showing improved form to win a ten-runner maiden at Pontefract (good) last time, travelling best before galloping on well to get up by a neck; this hot race for handicap debut demands plenty more of him but he brings clear potential.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Nosed ahead in the final strides of a maiden at Nottingham (1m, good) in May on second start; not so good and still looked inexperienced in a novice at Windsor (1m, good to firm) 18 days ago; this is a tough race for handicap debut but he's a scopey sort who should resume progress at some point.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Carried his head high in blinkers for last two starts but he challenged to win on the nod in a five-runner handicap at Newbury (1m3f, good to firm) last time, getting off the mark at the ninth attempt; up 3lb and into a much more competitive race, he could still be thereabouts but others make more appeal for win purposes.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won five of 15 races, including this month at Thirsk and Newmarket (both 1m4f on good to firm); Wednesday's 1m4f handicap here was a much sterner test of his credentials and he came up well short at 28-1, so others are again preferred.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Ended last season with a win here (7f, good) and started this one with creditable fourth of ten at Newbury; however, he faded right out of it at Newmarket (1m) next time and ended up nearly 10l behind Devil's Peak at Newbury (1m3f, good to firm) on latest start, which make him hard to fancy.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won at Windsor (11.4f, good to firm) in May in his fifth maiden race; last of three on handicap debut at Salisbury (1m4f, good to firm; Pearl River second) one month ago was probably better form but more is clearly needed from him; cheekpieces go on and latest start suggests 1m3f may suit him better.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Much improved on his first go in handicap company when emphatically landing a five-runner event at Nottingham (1m2f) in June; beaten a nose in a steadily run race at Newbury (1m2f, good to firm) three weeks ago and, off just 1lb higher, it's easy to think that this will suit him better.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Prevailed by half a length in Ayr handicap on Monday, registering an eighth turf win; incurs 4lb penalty but holds a solid chance in current form; gained his only AW success over C&D.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Failed to beat a rival in similar event over C&D in sole start (stable debut) this term; best watched unless the market suggests a better effort is likely; recorded sole win in turf seller.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Remains on a losing spell that goes back to his novice double in 2024 and has regressive results since switched to classified level, albeit perhaps needed latest run (back from break).

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Three handicap wins, including at Wolverhampton, for previous yard; 0-6 and hasn't shown the same form for current stable but latest effort (back here) wasn't devoid of promise as regards this drop to classified grade; possibilities.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Three wins for previous stable; 0-6 and inconsistent for current yard but has a good chance at the weights on classified debut, assuming this is one of her better days; shortlisted.

RaceName: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Record is only 2-36, the wins in AW handicaps in 2023 and 2024; has several pieces of classified form, beaten only 2l on turf last time, but again faces threats from class-droppers.

Won for the second time over hurdles when taking a 3m handicap at this meeting last year; pulled up in a Punchestown festival handicap on his only run since then; trainer won this with Intense Approach 12 months ago.
Point-to-point winner in 2023; poor hurdles form; has struggled in two outings over fences.

Winning hurdler over 2m4f on heavy; pick of six attempts chasing when worn down late in a 2m7f Limerick handicap last Christmas (soft-to-heavy) and when chasing home a useful sort in a Wexford beginners' event four weeks ago; trainer saddled a smart novice winner here on Tuesday.

Two hurdle wins in France in his early days; unconvincing chase form since his return from a long absence; made mistakes and was pulled up at Punchestown in June; previously blundered badly two out at Cork.

Plenty of chasing experience; has failed to build on a fine second behind Intense Approach in this race last year; best of his six subsequent starts when second in a handicap at last year's Listowel festival; pulled up at Roscommon last time, early mistake may have harmed his confidence; may bounce back to pose a threat now.
No luck in handicap hurdles since a Fairyhouse win in February; big task on chasing debut.

OwnerName: John P McManus & Mrs John Magnier
Spotlight: Beaten at short odds on debut in a bumper at this venue two years ago; won over hurdles at Roscommon last summer after a break; runner-up in a Listed novice here later that month, beaten by the subsequent County Hurdle second Sticktotheplan; ran out of steam on his reappearance in a 3m1f chase at Punchestown last month; likely to be at peak form now.

Useful juvenile hurdler the season before last; best run last term when fifth off 130 in a 2m4f handicap at Leopardstown; tailed off over 3m1f on chase debut; suffered the same fate over 2m at Wexford; not a betting proposition at the moment.
Low-rated hurdler/chaser; pulled up in a handicap chase at Punchestown last time; out of her depth here.

RaceName: Big Stage Hire Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Back in prime form at Southwell (1m4f, AW) last week, coming from off the pace for a clearcut success; raced only twice on turf (placed once) and untested on ground other than good but is 1lb ahead of the handicapper under her 5lb penalty and could still have untapped potential over this trip.

RaceName: Big Stage Hire Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Low-mileage 3yo who came second in both handicaps, at Wolverhampton (1m4f, AW) and Chepstow (1m2f, good to firm); tries a new trip here and probably still has more to offer.

RaceName: Big Stage Hire Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Well down the field in three 1m2f novice/maiden races in May/June and not obviously well treated for this handicap debut but combination of new trip and first-time cheekpieces may prompt improvement; market helpful.

OwnerName: The Jocks And The Geordies II
Spotlight: Only 1-32 and should have run better in a classified here last week as he stays 7f.

RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Three wins on AW last year but now on a losing run of 20; there have been some near misses during that sequence but not of late.

RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Classified Stakes
OwnerName: John And Tony Jarvis And Partner
Spotlight: All three wins have been on Tapeta so needs considering after some competitive runs on turf, though not drawn well.

RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Classified Stakes

RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Showed signs of a revival when fourth in a handicap at Thirsk (6f, good; 11-1) and a slow start was no help at Chester (stays 7f); only 2-35 but he's not without a chance.

RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Classified Stakes
