RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Sole win was at 7f but he's effective at 6f and could have a part to play if bouncing back from modest latest effort.

RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Classified Stakes
Spotlight: C&D handicap winner for Kevin Ryan in 2024; runner-up in a 5f classified at Southwell on yard debut but well held in a 6f handicap at Thirsk and he's been dealt a tough draw.

RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Not beaten far in her recent fourths, in a handicap (7f) and a classified race (7.6); something to prove on the AW and back at 6f, but looks up to winning a race of this nature, especially should the new blinkers assist.

RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Classified Stakes
Spotlight: No wins in 11 and ran no race last time at Thirsk; however, has placed form and would have a fair shout on these terms if back to anything like his best.

RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Beaten double-digit lengths in three 6f novice races but this is a lot easier and she's got a good pedigree.

RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Remains winless and hasn't been that threatening in any of her 12 defeats, especially of late; first classified assignment.

RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Classified Stakes
Spotlight: No wins in 11 and now with his third trainer; below best when last seen in March.

RaceName: Harry Potter Droneart Show Classified Stakes
Spotlight: No real sign of winning potential, including a 7f classified last time when in cheekpieces; now in blinkers.
0-10 and he was unable to reward market support on his stable debut at Ayr (1m2f, good) 26 days ago; new accessories given a spin this afternoon but he does have to prove his stamina.
Won minor events at Newcastle (1m2f, AW) and here (extended 1m4f, good) in June; reportedly bled from the nose in his hat-trick bid and then ran poorly at Newcastle last week; not easy to assess.
Two encouraging Flat runs for new stable, latterly when second of 11 at Pontefract (1m4f, good) 24 days ago; 1lb higher today but still holds stronger claims than many.
Three times a course winner for Jim Goldie, the latest (extended 1m4f) last August off a 9lb higher mark; solid efforts on her last three starts; big run expected.
Regressive 8yo who can't be recommended on this year's evidence.
Easy win at Southwell (1m4f, AW) in March but not at that level in six runs since; minor money perhaps his best hope.
Just one win (1m2f, AW) from his 24 starts but he arrives in good form, runner-up in three of his last four starts; should give his running once again.
Unplaced in 18 starts under both codes; plenty to prove.
42-race maiden who can't be recommended with confidence.

RaceName: Zyn In-The-Moment EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Seventh foal; closely related to three winners including Good Effort (prolific 5f-7f including Listed; RPR 114) and Crown Of Light (6f 2yo; 83), half-brother to two winners including Frostmagic (1m-1m4f; 82); dam unraced; yard has 35% record with 2yos this year and he needs watching in the market on debut.

RaceName: Zyn In-The-Moment EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Made a promising start when fourth at Newbury (6.5f, good to soft) last month but he failed to build on that when a well-held sixth at Lingfield (7f, AW) three weeks ago; others preferred.

RaceName: Zyn In-The-Moment EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 90,000gns yearling, 230,000gns breeze-up 2yo; first foal; dam unplaced 1m/9.4f (RPR 49), half-sister to winners Burnt Sugar (6f 2yo Group 3), Brown Sugar (5f/6f 2yo Group 3) and Vespasian (useful 5f-7f), out of useful 5f/6f winner; has plenty of speed in his pedigree and he needs a close look on debut.

RaceName: Zyn In-The-Moment EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 215,000euros breeze-up 2yo; only third of four on Carlisle debut (5f, good to firm) but he found lots of improvement when a clear second behind a smart rival who dominated at Ffos Las (6f, good) two weeks ago; sets a good standard on that form and this well-bred colt should have more to offer; key player.

RaceName: Zyn In-The-Moment EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Wootton Bassett colt who cost 180,000euros as a yearling; second foal; dam French 1m2f-11.5f winner (including Listed; RPR 106), half-sister to 5f Group 2 winner Soffia, out of Listed-placed 6f 2yo winning half-sister to 7f Group 3 winner Al Jazi; yard has won this in four of the last six years and he's an interesting newcomer.

RaceName: Zyn In-The-Moment EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 80,000gns yearling; ninth foal; closely related to 5f/7f winner Chartwell House (including 2yo/Australia; RPR 96), half-sister to four winners including Star Anthem (Group-placed 5f 2yo; 99) and Stratton Street (5f 2yo; 92); dam 6f winner (102); plenty to like on paper but this looks a tough starting point.

RaceName: Zyn In-The-Moment EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 160,000gns yearling; 7-2 outsider of three and came from last when runner-up over C&D (good to firm) last month, with all of them newcomers and there were just two necks between them; that was a promising start but she was beaten 9l over 7f here last time and has bit to prove after that.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: 8yo who made it eight wins from 48 starts when scoring on reappearance at Windsor (11.4f, good) in May; only third of seven there since (11.4f, good to firm) and may be vulnerable to younger legs today, but she's run well in the last two editions of this race and could do so again.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: After being progressive in handicaps (including on fast ground) she went very close in a C&D Listed race (soft) last month; soundly beaten in Group 2 at Newmarket (1m4f, good to firm) last time, when the trip wasn't an issue, but this 3yo is not ruled out back into a handicap.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo who hasn't been at her best this season but took a step back in the right direction when fourth of eight at Chester (10.3f, good) three weeks ago; she's well treated on the form shown at this meeting 12 months ago and it will be no surprise if she's in the mix.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Strong 2yo form here last summer and she reappeared with a conditions race win at Kempton (1m, AW) in March; she's had some tough assignments since but hasn't really kicked on and is not obviously well treated.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Handicap
OwnerName: Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum
Spotlight: Won three handicaps in a row in May/June at about 1m2f (good/soft) but she seems to have gone off the boil subsequently, finishing down the field in two handicaps and one Listed race; needs to get back on track.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Progressive since moving into handicaps in this hood and she made it 3-4 in such races when winning comfortably at Doncaster (1m2f, good to firm) three weeks ago; a 6lb rise may not stop her today.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Improved upon her first three runs (7f-8.6f) to win on handicap debut at Salisbury (1m2f, good to firm) three weeks ago when upped in trip in a first-time tongue-tie (retained); it was a small field but she came clear with an unexposed runner-up and she's just 2lb higher today; this 420,000gns yearling could have lots more to offer for her top yard.

Won twice over fences in 2025, most recently off 9lb lower at Leopardstown in December (2m1f, yielding); has come up short in three starts since, weakening on latest when upped to 2m5f in the Topham at Aintree; stamina a query upped further in trip.

1-6 over fences, the win coming in a mares' chase at Sligo last October; good runs in defeat the last twice in handicaps at Punchestown, beaten just 1.25l there on latest (2m4f, gd-yld) off 4lb lower; should go well, but has to definitively prove she stays this far.

Ended a long losing run when winning a nice pot at Limerick in December (2m3f, sft-hvy) off 4lb lower; modest efforts in three starts since and probably hasn't much wriggle room off current mark but has gone well here before, will like the ground and preferred by Cobden.

Won two of first three starts over fences, a beginners' at Downpatrick (19.5f, yld-sft) and a Kilbeggan handicap chase (20.5f, good) off 6lb lower; tame effort when pulled up over hurdles on latest and needs to rebound in first-time visor.

Prolific over hurdles (5-11) but is just 1-5 over fences; that win came over C&D (good) in a beginners' at this meeting last year (Donnie Devito third); lost way afterwards but given a break and should be sharper for a spin on the Flat at Bellewstown 29 days ago; not discounted in first-time blinkers.

Off the mark over fences at Limerick in March (2m2f, heavy) off 10lb lower; has backed that up with solid runs at Fairyhouse (2m5f, yld-sft) and when 4.25l behind Hermino AA at Roscommon (3m1f, soft); 5lb better off with that rival and kept ticking over with a spin on the Flat 11 days ago but might prefer it softer; blinkers on.

Things haven't gone to plan since a wide margin beginners' chase win at Wexford (3m1f, soft) in March; unseated and pulled up in handicaps at Punchestown and Kilbeggan; also beaten in three runner novice chase at Punchestown (3m1f, gd-yld); a bit to prove for now.

0-10 in chases but in the first three on five occasions, including when beaten a nose in this in 2024 off 3lb higher; generally struggled last season and no signs of revival on debut for this yard over timber at Kilbeggan in June; could be sharper for that, however, and worth market check in new visor.

Sole success over fences a mares beginners' at Ballinrobe in September 2024; ran respectably in the Mayo National last year but out of sorts in the autumn and miles behind a couple of these rivals on return from a break at Roscommon on latest.

Failed to complete in three of last four runs for Willie Mullins; modest start for this yard in the Midlands National, beaten 20l into sixth; this trip looks too sharp (sole chase win at 3m7f) and others have more convincing profiles.

Gained third chase win at Thurles in January by 0.75l off 8lb lower; soundly beaten off revised mark twice since and while trip and ground are fine here, the first-time tongue tie needs to eke out more.

2-4 over hurdles but remains a maiden over fences after nine runs and yet to trouble the judge; well held behind a few of these rivals in the Connacht National last time and a 3lb drop is not enough to tempt; preferred by Townend.

Signed off for Peter Fahey with an emphatic win over hurdles at Punchestown (16.5f, gd-yld) in October; bought for E25,000 in November and this course winner is worth a market check on debut for shrewd yard with a tongue tie and cheekpieces applied.

1-7 over fences; best run since his beginners' chase win at Down Royal (19.5f, good) last year came when a 3.75l third at Wexford in May (2m, gd-yld); disappointed in Summer Plate at Market Rasen latest; runner up in the QR handicap on the Flat here in 2024 so not totally discounted in new headgear combination.

2-7 over hurdles; 0-6 over fences but has run well in defeat, including when a close third behind Intense Approach in a C&D beginners' here last year; weighted to reverse that form and shaped promisingly in prep run after 218 days off at Wexford; could be on a nice mark for first handicap chase.

Back from a long spell in the doldrums to land the Connacht National at Roscommon (3m1f, yld-sft) in first-time blinkers (retained); hit with an 8lb rise for that and this ground may be on the quick side for him.

Off the mark over fences in emphatic fashion at Kilbeggan (20.5f, yielding) in May off 7lb lower; not beaten far in both starts since, including when just 2.75l behind the winner at Killarney latest (2m7f, good); yard had a winner here on Tuesday; should go well again.

0-9 over fences but has run well at times, including when a 1.5l second in this race last season for Gavin Cromwell; 2lb lower now and blew away the cobwebs after a 279-day break with a respectable run at Wexford earlier this month; preferred by O'Keeffe and an interesting runner.

Hasn't won over fences since 2023 but comes into this in good form; beaten just a neck in a Kilbeggan handicap chase (20.5f, good) on latest; raised 1lb for that and this is tougher but has run well on both previous visits to this venue so not totally discounted.

Off the mark over fences in a Kilbeggan beginners' on latest (25.5f, good), pulling clear to score by 9l; raised 6lb for that effort but has placed off this sort of mark before and the drop back in trip shouldn't pose any problems; player.

RaceName: Trusted Betting Site Reviews gambling.com British EBF Restricted Novice (Bands B-D) (Qual) (GBB)
Spotlight: Bullt upon encouraging debut when leading close home to pip Tricky Jenny here (5f, firm) this month; didn't get a clear run that day and has scope for further progress over this longer trip; respected under penalty.

RaceName: Trusted Betting Site Reviews gambling.com British EBF Restricted Novice (Bands B-D) (Qual) (GBB)
Spotlight: Not beaten far when fifth of eight on debut at Wolverhampton (5f, AW) in April but both subsequent runs (5f/6f) were disappointing; needs last month's wind op to have made a difference.

RaceName: Trusted Betting Site Reviews gambling.com British EBF Restricted Novice (Bands B-D) (Qual) (GBB)
Spotlight: Close second in Musselburgh seller (5f, good) last month and made the frame in both subsequent nurseries, albeit it's tricky to gauge what she achieved when second of three behind a 1-4 favourite last time; goes beyond a bare 5f for first time here; ought to be very competitive on these terms.

RaceName: Trusted Betting Site Reviews gambling.com British EBF Restricted Novice (Bands B-D) (Qual) (GBB)
Spotlight: Soundly beaten on debut in June (6f) but belied 150-1 odds when very close second over C&D (firm) at start of this month and has a big role to play if in similar form again.

RaceName: Trusted Betting Site Reviews gambling.com British EBF Restricted Novice (Bands B-D) (Qual) (GBB)
Spotlight: Second foal; dam prolific 1m-1m2f winner (RPR 74), half-sister to a French 6.7f 2yo winner; rare 2yo runner for the stable.

RaceName: Trusted Betting Site Reviews gambling.com British EBF Restricted Novice (Bands B-D) (Qual) (GBB)
OwnerName: M Reddy, J Mallon, N J Clayton & Partner
Spotlight: Never dangerous when eighth of ten on debut at Chepstow (6f, good to firm) a week ago; remains best watched.

RaceName: Trusted Betting Site Reviews gambling.com British EBF Restricted Novice (Bands B-D) (Qual) (GBB)
Spotlight: Raced too freely and disappointing on last month's AW debut (6f) but lost out only by a nose to Sheer Beauty when back on turf here (5f, firm) 16 days ago and is 7lb better off with her this time; obvious claims.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Mrs T Burns And Rjh Ltd
Spotlight: £16,000 yearling; second foal; half-brother to 6f 2yo winner Magistery (RPR 67); dam 7f winner (including 2yo; 95), half-sister to winners Sergeant Wilko (useful 5f 2yo/6f), Stately Home (1m) and Mister Guerrieri (Italian 5f/5.5f); stable have a smart 2yo in their ranks; betting revealing.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Shaped well in a useful seller at York (6f, good) on debut; beaten favourite at Redcar (7f, good to firm) 12 days ago but still ran to a similar level; should go well again.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Not far behind Gerry's Darling and Hey Up Ronnie at Redcar (7f, good to firm) on his debut 12 days ago; open to improvement but it is slightly disconcerting to see headgear reached for so quickly.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Down the field in both starts, including behind three of today's rivals at Redcar 12 days ago; hard to fancy.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Down the field on her first two starts but she took a good step forward when keeping on for second at Redcar (7f, good to firm) 12 days ago; finished in front of three of today's rivals on that occasion and she may do so again.

RaceName: Zyn Pacesetter Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Study Of Man half-sister to four winners, notably Ebury (1m; RPR 100); dam 1m4f scorer (82), closely related to Derby runner-up Dragon Dancer; 100-30 on Salisbury debut (1m2f, good to firm) last month and she made virtually all before winning by 3l; that was a bright start and she sets a good standard under a penalty.

RaceName: Zyn Pacesetter Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Fourth foal; half-sister to winners Island Bandit (7f/1m; RPR 88) and Brave Call (1m-1m4f including Australia; 86); dam placed 1m2f (78), half-sister to useful 1m winner Clemmie C; has good standard to aim at on debut and she could be one for later on.

RaceName: Zyn Pacesetter Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
OwnerName: L J Vaessen And Stephen Barber
Spotlight: Showed some promise on her third start when runner-up here (1m, good to firm; 33-1) two weeks ago but she was beaten 4l and that form is modest; still early days but she has plenty to find with Aleatrix and needs another big step forward at this new trip.

RaceName: Zyn Pacesetter Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 125,000gns foal, 240,000gns yearling; eighth foal; half-sister to three winners including Emily Upjohn (9.4f-1m4f including Group 1 Coronation Cup; RPR 123) and Mushaireb (7f/1m including Australia; 91); dam 1m2f winner (97), sister to 1m2f Group 3 winner Hazarista; interesting newcomer for the Gosdens and she needs a close look.

Won a 1m2f (gd-yld) Curragh premier handicap off 15lb lower last September and followed up in a Listed heat at Leopardstown (1m2f, heavy); no impact when slowly away in three runs in Listed and Group 2 company this season; may be on tough mark back in a handicap.

Hasn't won since landing premier handicap at the Curragh in October 2024 (1m2f, good); remains 6lb above that last success but shaped as though coming back to form at the Curragh on latest and ran well at this meeting in 2023 and 2024; could go well.

Group 3 winner ran a huge race in the Cesarewitch at Newmarket (2m2f, gd-fm) last October, beaten just 1.25l into second; just 1lb higher here but hasn't really fired in three runs this term and this trip looks on the sharp side.

Gained third career win on latest at Down Royal (10.5f, soft), bolting up by 6.5l; handicapper took a dim view, hiking her up 14lb; this longer trip is fine, as is quicker ground, but a big career best will be needed to follow up in this tougher race; drawn wide.

OwnerName: Westerberg & Mrs Magnier & M Tabor & D Smith
Spotlight: 3yo won a 1m maiden (gd-yld) at Punchestown last September; fine run behind Derby winner Christmas Day in a Leopardstown Group 3 in October (1m1f, yielding); not disgraced in London Gold Cup on seasonal return but bombed out in Ascot Group 2 on latest; others preferred.

3-3 on the AW but effective on turf and won easily on return from a 107 day break at Leopardstown in May (1m4f, good) off 8lb lower; had excuse when third of 13 (1.75l behind This Songisforyou) off revised mark at the Curragh latest (fly leapt from stalls); well-drawn here and in the mix once he behaves himself at the start.

AW winner got off the mark on turf at the Curragh (1m2f, gd-fm) on latest 34 days ago; rider was taking off 7lb that day so with a 9lb rise, he's effectively 16lb higher here; however, this longer trip could unlock further improvement so not written off.

Ran poorly over hurdles at Listowel in May but last two runs on the Flat have been decent; 4l second of 10 at Leopardstown in early May (1m4f, good); 4.75l fourth of 12 at the Curragh 34 days ago; place claims off 1lb lower but needs to find a bit more to win.

Good first effort for this yard when narrowly denied in the Chester Plate (18.5f, good); led and weakened into ninth of 24 off this mark in a Curragh handicap on latest (1m6f, good); drops in trip now and cheekpieces go on; favourable draw.
Won over hurdles at Wexford in May; below best in that sphere twice since and was well beaten in this race last year; 4lb lower now but others appeal more.
Two-time AW winner is 0-9 on turf; stayed on well for a 2.75l second over 2m1f at Killarney last time and closely matched with The Kingstonian on Chester form in May; may need more of a stamina test.

3yo signed off last season with a Gowran maiden win (8.5f, heavy); narrowly denied by subsequent Queen's Vase winner Limestone on seasonal return in 3yo race at Cork (10.5f, gd-yld); not disgraced in Curragh Group 3 on latest (1m2f, good) and now makes handicap debut; could be on a nice mark based on his Cork form.

OwnerName: Team Valor International LLC & Gary Barber
Spotlight: 3yo has won two of his four starts; scored in a Curragh maiden on debut (7f, good); came from the back to score by 1.25l in a valuable Leopardstown handicap on latest (1m1f, good) and the runner up was a big eyecatcher at Goodwood on Tuesday; should stay 1m4f on breeding but 3yos haven't got a great record in this race and he's 9lb higher now.

Three-time winner on the Flat, including over C&D last October, but all four wins have come on soft and heavy ground; excellent second in the Cork Derby (1m4f, soft) when last seen in May; just 1lb higher here but needs rain.

2-12 on the Flat, both wins coming at Down Royal over 10.5f (good) and 1m5f (yielding) last season; not beaten far in the Cork Derby in May and traffic problems when a 9.5l fourth at the Curragh latest; others look better treated.

Gained second Flat win when bolting up over 1m6f at Fairyhouse last month on return from a 143-day break; hit hard for that with a 14lb rise, drops back in trip and this is a much deeper race; drawn wide but could be more to come.

In fine form on turf and on the AW in 2026; has won three of last five starts, most recently on penultimate start at Limerick (12.5f, soft) off 4lb lower; 2m1f may have stretched at Killarney latest and drops back in trip now; place shout.

Loves it when the mud is flying, just as it was when she won off 9lb lower at Gowran in October (1m4f, heavy); has run respectably on all four starts on her favoured ground this term and has gone well here before but this ground will surely be too lively for her.

RaceName: Bath Rum And Reggae Race Night 15th August Classified Stakes (Bath Summer Sprint Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Has poor 1-52 strike-rate, the win gained on Polytrack (5f) in 2023; recent efforts have been underwhelming and he makes very limited appeal.

RaceName: Bath Rum And Reggae Race Night 15th August Classified Stakes (Bath Summer Sprint Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Placed for first time in seven-race career when coming from off the pace for third in similar C&D race to this last month (good ground); that was his turf debut and he could plausibly still have a bigger run in him if today's faster ground suits.

RaceName: Bath Rum And Reggae Race Night 15th August Classified Stakes (Bath Summer Sprint Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Ex-Irish mare who went close in this grade at Nottingham (5f, good to firm) a fortnight ago, on her third start for Adrian Wintle, and ought to be better suited by this longer trip; likely contender.

RaceName: Bath Rum And Reggae Race Night 15th August Classified Stakes (Bath Summer Sprint Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Made quite encouraging seasonal debut in C&D handicap (good to firm; first-time cheekpieces) in May but has not built on that on either start since, and was behind Jackie Brown when fifth in this grade at Nottingham (5f, good to firm) a fortnight ago.

RaceName: Bath Rum And Reggae Race Night 15th August Classified Stakes (Bath Summer Sprint Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Gained three of his nine wins here, two on firm ground over this trip; kept on for second (no match for winner) off his basement handicap mark over C&D (firm) at start of this month and has each-way claims again.

RaceName: Bath Rum And Reggae Race Night 15th August Classified Stakes (Bath Summer Sprint Series Qualifier)
OwnerName: Mrs S M Maine & Roger Gould & Partner
Spotlight: Nine-time winner who was beaten only by two necks when third in Class 5 Chepstow handicap (6f, good to firm) a fortnight ago; also suited by this C&D and commands respect on first dip into this basement grade.

RaceName: Bath Rum And Reggae Race Night 15th August Classified Stakes (Bath Summer Sprint Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Runner-up over C&D (good) and at Brighton (7f, good to firm) in refitted cheekpieces last month and has obvious claims if judged on those efforts but didn't fire on her latest outing and her overall profile is regressive; others preferred.

RaceName: Bath Rum And Reggae Race Night 15th August Classified Stakes (Bath Summer Sprint Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Third in similar C&D race to this (good; first run since rejoining this stable) in June and also ran well when third in recent 5f handicap here (firm) but is not one to rely upon heavily and sometimes races too freely.

RaceName: Bath Rum And Reggae Race Night 15th August Classified Stakes (Bath Summer Sprint Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Gained his only win on Polytrack (5f) but was placed in this grade at Leicester (6f, good to firm) this month and has now made the frame on his last three turf starts (one was over C&D); must be considered.

RaceName: Bernard Hunter Mobile Cranes Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Improved for the switch to nurseries and/or 7f when a front-running second of four at Catterick last week; could do with settling better but he is 3lb ahead of the handicapper and needs taking seriously.

RaceName: Bernard Hunter Mobile Cranes Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Gelded after his second start and duly showed improvement by finishing fourth of 11 in a novice at Ripon (6f, good); moves into nurseries with the potential for better; new trip; check betting.

RaceName: Bernard Hunter Mobile Cranes Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Off the mark at the fifth attempt when landing a C&D seller last month; went down fighting in a Beverley nursery two weeks later and she should make another bold bid despite her 3lb rise.

RaceName: Bernard Hunter Mobile Cranes Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Ran well for second at Newcastle (7f, AW) last month but she finished out the back on her nursery debut at Leicester 17 days ago; risky.

RaceName: Bernard Hunter Mobile Cranes Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Big prices for her three starts but she has shown promise on the last two occasions, third of ten upped to 7f at Ayr this month; can continue to progress.

RaceName: Bernard Hunter Mobile Cranes Nursery Handicap
OwnerName: Nick Bradley Racing 13 & P J Makin
Spotlight: 2lb better off with Amantha for a short-head defeat over C&D last month; low-key nursery debut last week where she was reportedly unsuited by the fast ground; still early days.

RaceName: Bernard Hunter Mobile Cranes Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: She has finished third in her two nursery runs this month, running creditably but failing to improve for the addition of cheekpieces at Leicester 17 days ago; needs more to take this.

Recorded his 13th turf win when scoring in good style at Haydock (6f, good to firm) in April; struggled at York last time but that was a highly competitive Class 4 event and he was runner-up here (5f, good to firm) on his penultimate run; has claims if he can recapture that form and he's not ruled out on this drop back in grade.

7yo who often ran well in the US, albeit winning just once (6.5f, firm) back in 2023; sent off at 80-1 on British/stable debut over C&D last month and he faded into ninth of ten; wasn't beaten far on that reappearance run but others are preferred.

His last three wins have been over C&D and latest was in a Class 4 on good to firm 13 days ago; that was a narrow success but he finished well to beat the favourite and is only 2lb higher here; respected.

His last win was almost two years ago but he's well treated on old form and showed signs of a revival with blinkers added when fourth at Windsor (6f, good to firm) last time; usually comes from off the pace and could be dangerous if he gets the breaks.

Ended his abbreviated campaign last season with a win in this race; well held in his first three runs this term but he turned things around with a near-miss at Newbury (6f, good to firm) three weeks ago; nudged up 2lb but he remains feasibly treated and is respected back at this track.

Off the mark at the ninth attempt when justifying 13-8 favouritism with a comfortable win at Nottingham (6f, good to firm) two weeks ago; up 7lb but that was a personal best last time and he's still unexposed at this trip; key player.

Won on the other course here (6f, good to firm) last May but he's been up and down since and has been out of sorts in his last two starts; now 8lb lower than for his last success but he needs a major revival with cheekpieces added.

OwnerName: J Sarkar, D Sarkar, O Sarkar & D Sarkar
Spotlight: Dual 7f winner last summer (good to firm/AW) but he's been well held in both runs this season including over C&D; now back on his last winning mark but he needs to turn things around.

Well held in five runs for Jane Chapple-Hyam including a handicap on the Rowley course here (1m, good) in May; changed hands for 6,000gns since; still early days but she needs improvement dropped to 6f on her stable debut; hood added.
26-race maiden who returned after a long absence in March and he's been tailed off in his last two runs; long way out of the weights here and he can only be watched; headgear removed.

OwnerName: Mrs Paul Shanahan & Mrs Wendy O'Leary
Spotlight: Fair debut over 7f, well beaten on second start; does not appeal against younger rivals.
Last of five at Killarney on belated debut; can be left out of calculations.
Placed in bumpers; 102-rated winning hurdler; remote sixth on Flat debut at Roscommon in May.

Three-time winner over hurdles; creditable second on recent Flat debut at Ballinrobe, though beaten 8l in a race of lower standard than this; now has to take on younger rivals and will need to find plenty of improvement.

Bumper winner; recorded a second hurdles win when beating Paul Townend's Galway Hurdle mount Murcia at Killarney; beaten 21l in seventh in a C&D maiden for amateur riders here on Wednesday; may get closer this time.
Ran twice for Dermot Weld late last season; should be more mature now but unlikely to be good enough on stable debut; visored.
55-rated filly. minor placed form on AW in Britain; no apparent chance in a maiden.

OwnerName: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith
Spotlight: Frankel filly is closely related to Group 1 winners Hydrangea, The United States and Hermosa; limited sort but a a breakthrough win looks on the cards following Fairyhouse second; Pleased back in fourth then.
Eighth foal; half-sister by Elusive Pimpernel to three winners on the continent; dam unraced half-sister to 7f 2yo/1m4f winner; best watched on debut.
Phoenix Of Spain filly out of an unraced mare; hooded and apprentice-ridden for debut.
Has shown ability in her two outings; 5l to find with Pleased on Fairyhouse running; more likely a handicap prospect.
Finished with only one behind her in a Limerick race in which Stellar Moment was second.

Made an encouraging Limerick debut in April, third behind an odds-on stablemate; still looked a bit raw when second (again behind a shorter-priced stablemate) at the Curragh; not certain to uphold that form with Porters Corner and has a bit to find with Cosmetic on Fairyhouse running last time.

Signs of inexperience on debut at the Curragh; did well to finish third, only one length behind today's rival Pleased; cheekpieces may help, and it will be no surprise if she turns the tables on the runner-up.
Improved from debut when a staying-on third over 1m2f at Leopardstown; saw out this trip well enough when second at Limerick; not much improvement needed to win a maiden.
Beaten 21l on debut over 7f at Leopardstown last October; huge improvement needed.

RaceName: Compare Betting Sites At gambling.com Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B-D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Left James Tate after finishing down the field over C&D (soft) on debut in September; returns having been gelded; might be seen to better effect on today's faster ground but is not the percentage call.

RaceName: Compare Betting Sites At gambling.com Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B-D) (GBB Race)
OwnerName: Mrs Wendy Jarrett & J S Moore
Spotlight: A big-priced outsider for recent debut at Ffos Las (5f, good) but shaped with promise before fading into fifth of seven; ought to have learnt from that experience and this race looks easier; can make his presence felt.

RaceName: Compare Betting Sites At gambling.com Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B-D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Raced far too freely and showed only minor promise on her first two starts (both 6f); open to improvement at some stage but will remain a risky option until she learns to settle.

RaceName: Compare Betting Sites At gambling.com Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B-D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Showed some improvement and ran well from the front when third at Nottingham (6f, good to firm) ten days ago, her fourth start ought to be a tough nut to crack here.

RaceName: Compare Betting Sites At gambling.com Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B-D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Looks pretty exposed after seven starts but has made the frame in two run-of-the-mill handicaps for her new stable this month (6f/5f) and has a decent chance at the weights here; sports first-time cheekpieces.

RaceName: Compare Betting Sites At gambling.com Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B-D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Struggled at triple-digit odds in two 1m novice races in May/June (hung violently left-handed last time); now tries sprinting.

C&D winner; it has been a while since his latest success but he has slipped down the weights and both this year's C&D runs (in deeper races) were encouraging; can go well fresh and a big run is on the cards.

Off the mark for the year when comfortably winning a C&D handicap last month; two good efforts have followed, running well in the circumstances when third at Newmarket (5f, good to firm) four weeks ago; the stalls can be an issue but he should be bang there if breaking on terms.
Useful 2yo; it has been a struggle more recently but he is dropping down the weights and appeals as the type to come good soon; that may coincide with him tackling slower ground though.

OwnerName: B Jordan, Brian Jordan, S Jordan & N McConnell
Spotlight: Often promised better as a 3yo; ran well over C&D on his reappearance in April and confirmed that promise by seeing off 16 rivals here eight days later; his progress has stalled more recently but it wouldn't be a great surprise to see him return to form back at Musselburgh.

OwnerName: Ursa Major Racing Ltd And Partner
Spotlight: Won the corresponding race 12 months ago off 6lb higher; back to winning ways when seeing off ten rivals at Ayr (5f, good to firm; made all) 18 days ago; this is a higher grade but the horse he beat last time ran well at Goodwood on Tuesday; not ruled out.

His last win was was in 2023 but that was a Group 3 event and he went close behind Where's Freddy over C&D (good to firm; 3-1 favourite) 13 days ago; on same mark here and he's a big player if he can repeat that form; visor added.

Front-runner who ended a long losing run with a dominant display over C&D (good) last month; struggled on his return visit three weeks ago but that was the Bunbury Cup and he remains well treated on his old form; respected on this big drop back in grade.

Ex-French gelding who has raced mainly at about 1m but he ran well to finish fourth in a C&D handicap (good to firm) three weeks ago; needs to build on that but he hasn't been with the Gosdens for long and this is a drop back in grade.

In-form 7yo who has reached the frame in his last three runs including when third of 11 in a C&D handicap (good to firm) three weeks ago; finished ahead of Exposure in that race and he has each-way claims again.

Responded well to first-time cheekpieces when winning over C&D (good) last month but he was well held back here (fifth of seven) 13 days ago; finished behind some of today's rivals in that race and he needs to step up again after that.

All four turf wins have been gained on this course (7f/1m); beaten around 9l in his first two runs this season but he returned to form when beating Jumby over C&D (good to firm) 13 days ago; only 2lb higher here and has leading claims if he can back that up.

Versatile sort who was runner-up at Chester (12.3f, good) in May but she's not easy to predict and was tailed off in the Kensington Palace at Royal Ascot (1m, good to firm) last time; back in calmer waters now but she looks weighted near best off this mark and others are preferred.

Won on the other course here (7f, good) in May and he's finished runner-up over C&D and at Epsom (7f, good to firm) in last two starts; was beaten 3l last time but that was behind an improver and he's 1lb lower here; possibilities.

Front-runner who has won five of his last seven starts but all of those were in Class 6 events and he was only third of six when well treated under a penalty at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm) last time; 6lb higher here and he has some work to do in this competitive race.
Ordinary maiden form; 33-1 when last of eight over 1m at Killarney in his first handicap; huge task against that background.

Profited from return to soft ground when making all over 1m at Leopardstown, winning cosily by 5l from Cosmic Funk; fair third behind the ultra-progressive Meriden at the same venue on next start; struggled on good ground at Fairyhouse; any further ease would help.
Ran poorly at Fairyhouse in June; that outing may have come too soon after a Gowran win four days earlier in first-time cheekpieces (discarded now).
Three maiden runs over varying trips; 1m effort at the Curragh was reasonably encouraging, so perhaps this will prove close to his optimum.
Fair runs in maidens before stepping up in trip for handicap debut at Down Royal, beaten 8l in third over 1m2f; did not quite get home over 1m4f at Limerick; high draw could make things difficult.
Looked in need of further when running over 6f at Navan on handicap debut; open to improvement, and cheekpieces may help.

Highlight of juvenile form was a 7f course nursery win on heavy, achieved at the main expense of today's rival Aquilla Star; hard to be confident after a below-par Leopardstown run in June; would benefit from rain.
Not an obvious contender on three runs in maidens between March and May; still early days, may improve.
Uneven form for Ken Condon at two; made the frame three times and showed enough to imply that she is a potentially interesting runner for a trainer who targets this meeting astutely.
Best of three runs last season was at this venue; big price when down the field at Fairyhouse on her handicap/seasonal debut; major improvement needed.

Runner-up to Down The Glen in a heavy ground nursery over 7f here last October; failed to cut much ice on her seasonal debut at Down Royal last month; much better when losing out by only a neck at Ballinrobe 11 days ago; first-time cheekpieces; definite chance.

Some promise in maidens before second on handicap debut at Leopardstown; found to be coughing post-race after a lesser run on next start; fifth in a claimer at Killarney last time, one length behind Love Orchid; his new trainer fits him with cheekpieces.
Progressed to win a Dundalk nursery last December; might just have needed the run when fading late at Fairyhouse early this month; has a bit to find with third-placed JP's Express.
Showed much-improved form when 33-1 third at Fairyhouse early this month; the winner Kirkland Sioux backed that up with a Curragh win; cheekpieces on for the first time now.
Gained a breakthrough win at Wolverhampton last December; subsequent placed form in small-field events; worth considering on the strength of a recent second at Pontefract.
Down the field in a claimer at Killarney, with Love Orchid and Cosmic Funk among those in front of her; 5lb higher than for Gowran win in May; tongue-tie for the first time.
Some signs of ability in maidens at two; fourth in a claimer at Killarney on latest; needs to improve on this term's handicap form.

RaceName: Thank You Great Western Air Ambulance Handicap
Spotlight: Perhaps best known as a Chepstow regular but this track also suits her; yet to win this season but has been placed three times (5f/7f) and her current mark is workable; no surprise if she features.

RaceName: Thank You Great Western Air Ambulance Handicap
Spotlight: Northern raider who has won twice on fast ground over 5f this season; had poor track position when below form at Beverley recently; no surprise if he bounces back quickly over this slightly longer trip.

RaceName: Thank You Great Western Air Ambulance Handicap
Spotlight: Has much better strike-rate on AW but recovered from slow start to win here (5f, firm) on turf return in May, and this longer trip will arguably suit him better; needs to bounce back from two down-the-field runs but was denied a clear run on first occasion; can't be ruled out.

RaceName: Thank You Great Western Air Ambulance Handicap
OwnerName: Homecroft Wealth, Paul J Dixon & Partners
Spotlight: Three-time AW who ran well from the front when second at Wolverhampton (6f, AW) ten days ago; 0-13 on turf but remains 6lb lower than when second over C&D (firm) in May; could be hard to catch.

RaceName: Thank You Great Western Air Ambulance Handicap
Spotlight: 12-race maiden; not disgraced when fifth of seven behind Nordic Glory here (5f, firm) on seasonal debut in May but a lesser effort over C&D followed and others in this field have much stronger claims; tongue-tie removed after one use.
Not fired in two runs back from a 399-day absence; has won at this track and he is on a handy mark so not impossible he'll bounce back, for all the trip is on the sharp side.
His three turf wins have come around the right-hand turn at Beverley; twice a runner-up in May but his form has dipped twice since; has the ability to feature at this level.
Kept on for second at Carlisle (6f, good) on her handicap debut last month; ran poorly at Ayr three weeks later; now steps up in trip with a point to prove.

Two 7f AW wins this year; had few chances on turf but he has run well at Catterick in the past, including last month; still looked in top form when meeting trouble in running at Wolverhampton last time; contender.
This C&D brings out the best in him and he had a near miss here last month; neither Ayr run this month has been comparable but he should be in the shake up back here.
Over three years since her last win but she has run with credit on her last three starts; others still preferred for win purposes.
Exposed maiden but she has run with credit in two 6f handicaps this summer, finishing second of seven at Catterick last week; returning to 7f will be in her favour and she is high on the list.

All six wins have come on AW and latest was off 3lb lower at Wolverhampton (1m6f) last November; 0-12 on turf but she gave it a good shot under a prominent ride when third of 11 at Carlisle (1m6f, good) last month; now drops back in trip but she's a player if she can find a bit extra.

Improved her record 4-7 when coming from rear to score on her comeback at Windsor (11.5f, good to firm) in May; held in last three runs but she ran into two progressive 3yos in a Class 3 at Ascot last time; looks interesting on this big drop back in grade and she won in some tactical events last season.

20-1 winner off 4lb lower at Epsom (1m2f, good) last August in her second handicap; runner-up on next two starts but much less impact since and she's finished down the field in her four runs this season; overall record is now 1-12 and she has something to prove at this new trip.

Five-race maiden but she was beaten less than 2l when third of five in an Epsom handicap (1m4f, good to firm) three weeks ago; was allowed to set a slow pace but she still has potential and could make a serious impact if she can build on that last run.

Her standout effort in maiden/novice events was a 4l fourth of seven at Bath (1m2f, good to firm) on her penultimate run; opening mark looks on the high side but it's still early days and she's a possible improver on this step up in trip (dam a Listed-placed 1m4f-12.5f winner).

OwnerName: Athlumney Farms Ltd & Eoin Baxter & Mrs M D O'Callaghan
Spotlight: Won Ballinrobe claimer last summer; finished the season with second over 2m at Dundalk; absent since an early-season Navan run, fair third in a 1m2f event on heavy; longer trip and better ground should help her cause.

Won twice at Leopardstown track last year over 1m4f/1m5f; has confirmed a liking for that venue this season; third to today's rival Cooley's Mist in a 1m5f event the middle of the month, as a prelude to last week's winning effort over 1m7f; up 5lb, can remain competitive.
Recorded his third AW win recently; placed only once from eight starts on turf; declared to run in the 5.40 on Thursday.

Produced back-to-back solid runs at Ballinrobe and the Curragh earlier this season; failed to reach the same standard in his next four races; had plenty to spare when winning over an extended 1m1f at Gowran last Saturday; unknown quantity at this trip, good chance if he stays.
Beat Coulstys Way in this race last year, completing a hat-trick of staying handicap wins in the process; placed over hurdles this month; may be peaking at the right time.
Two Flat wins in Germany early in his career, and Listed-placed; can be rated a possible future handicap hurdle winner on recent form; potentially interesting back on the Flat now.
Won twice last year, including a defeat of Quiz Test at the Curragh; has failed to find his best form this season.
Winning favourite over 1m5f at Leopardstown recently after two third placings; improving type; cheekpieces added after a winning display.

Three-time winner at 1m2f on soft or heavy, latest over two years ago; fair form this season and proved he can stay when second at 33-1 over 2m1f at Limerick last month; below that level at Tramore last time.

Sole win came at Cork in 2023; decent form last autumn, including a close third over 1m4f at this venue and second in a 19-runner contest at the Curragh; made the frame at Gowran and Limerick recently; no stamina concerns.

In good form last summer, winning at Roscommon (1m4f, good) and second behind Steps In The Sand in this event; pleasing effort when third at Killarney on her second start of the season; one for the shortlist.
Took a big rise in the ratings for a 15l Roscommon win last season; unplaced in two early-season outings; blinkered  first time; still a bit high in handicap.
Has hinted at winning potential; hard to fancy after a disappointing handicap debut (last of six) at Limerick.

Ordinary form in maidens; little impact in his first two handicaps; took a step in the right direction when second to Nermal at Roscommon; staying on well when third here on Tuesday; longer trip and hood may help.
Good effort in a 1m4f maiden at Limerick last time; previously fifth in a handicap at the same venue; may find some improvement over this trip
Placed for the first time at Down Royal last month but soundly beaten, needs to find extra; trainer also runs Blissful Bonita.

Gained all ten wins at this track, the latest in 1m classified at start of this month; close second in handicap over that trip here (again on firm) a fortnight later and will be fine back over 1m2f but recent 4lb rise might leave this 8yo a shade vulnerable.

Now 2lb lower than when going close at Chepstow (1m, good) last month and will also be suited by today's longer trip but this regressive and inconsistent 6yo is on a long losing run, and his habit of starting slowly is always a worry.
Won three times last summer (twice over 11.6f on fast ground here) but has been soundly beaten on all three starts since returning from a break in June; needs to turn things around.
Managed only sixth of nine when upped to 1m2f at Ffos Las (good) this month and has now been unplaced all seven starts; needs help from the new cheekpieces.
Eight-race maiden who was allowed to set a steady pace when fourth of nine at Chepstow (1m2f, good to firm) a week ago and is effectively 1lb higher here; needs to take a step forward.

Showed no significant promise as a 2yo (four runs; 6f-1m) and is out of the weights for this seasonal debut but had wind surgery in March and wouldn't be the first from her stable to show huge improvement once switched to a middle-distance handicap as a 3yo.

Two solid efforts for new stable, latterly beaten a short head into second at Ayr (1m5f, good to firm) 18 days ago; twice a winner over hurdles but this will be the first time he has tackled 2m on the Flat.
Modest hurdle form for this yard, albeit he was returning from 343 days off when third at Hexham last month; had fair Flat form in Ireland in his youth but does come with risk attached.

OwnerName: Mr & Mrs G F Hall Racing
Spotlight: On a losing run and her latest Catterick second came in a four-runner race; she will need more to come out on top this time.
Three course wins over shorter but does stay this trip; mixed bag so far this year and he needs a recent stable switch (same owner) to spark something extra.
Improved for the switch to handicaps this year, making all for wins over C&D and at Ayr (1m7f, soft); there could well be more in the tank and he's a strong contender despite his latest 4lb rise.
Two wins this summer, including C&D, and he wasn't beaten far at Ayr (1m5f, good to firm) 18 days ago; stable may have stronger claims with Gallus Norman.

His first five wins were on AW but he's won twice at Yarmouth this summer including an emphatic success over 1m (good to firm; cheekpieces added) last week; has a penalty but that was a personal best last time and he's strongly respected.

Doubled his tally on turf with big-field amateur riders' win at Doncaster (good to soft) in March and he scored again at Thirsk (also 1m, good to firm) in May; was better than ever with those wins but he's not threatened in his last three starts and he's still 5lb higher than for his last success; others are more persuasive.

Can miss the break and has a patchy profile; bounced back with a close second over C&D (good to firm) last month but she hung left when fourth of six here (7f, good to firm) last time; hood is now added on this step back up in trip but she comes with risks attached.

Unexposed gelding who has form figures of 211 in handicaps and who has won by 5l at Windsor (1m, good to firm) and Carlisle (1m, good) in those last two runs; up another 11lb but he still looks feasibly on his latest form and is open to more progress; major player.

His two Flat wins have been over 1m6f and 2m on AW; won over hurdles at Worcester last summer but he's been generally disappointing since, including in two Flat runs (1m2f/11.4f) this season; has plenty to prove and his tactical speed will be tested back at this trip.

Has turned things around with cheekpieces added this summer, finishing runner-up at Yarmouth (1m, good to firm) before scoring in similar conditions over C&D six weeks ago; this is tougher off 3lb higher but that was a brave win last time and he remains well treated on his old form; shortlisted.

Won two AW handicaps for George Scott in March; fair efforts in the last two of his three runs for current yard but his latest second was in a three-runner race at Nottingham (1m2f, good to firm); this drop back in trip could suit but he needs to find more to make the breakthrough on turf.

Took the scalp of Daddy Long Legs on Flat debut at Down Royal (1m5f, soft); may have used too much petrol to get to the front early when fading into fourth in a Listed heat at Roscommon on latest; not discounted with sights lowered.

8yo has won this race for the past two years on soft and yielding ground; soundly beaten in both starts in handicaps this term, but connections have likely targeted this race and could make a bold bid.

Six-time course winner bounced back to form with an excellent effort in the QR handicap here on Monday, beaten just 1.25l off 88; this trip possibly on the sharp side but loves it here and not discounted for place purposes.

Top rated here at 105 and this three-time winner ran a very respectable race in a Listed contest at Limerick (12.5f, soft) on return from break on latest; won over this trip at Killarney in 2024 and ground versatile (won Queen Alexandra at Ascot in 2024 on gd-fm); the one to beat if running to his rating.
Modest jumper (rated 99) is 0-2 on the Flat and rates an unlikely winner based on her latest two runs in maidens at Tramore and Ballinrobe.

OwnerName: Annus Mirabilis Synd'/Sean O'Driscoll/Middle Cow Unlimited
Spotlight: Best on very testing ground and was well held in the QR handicap here on Monday when 8.5l behind Teed Up; big swing in the weights with that rival but would make more appeal if the ground was heavy; cheekpieces go on.

Prominent racer; the winner of two of his last four starts, latterly a 5f handicap at Hamilton (good) three weeks ago; that form has already received several boosts and a 2lb rise looks lenient; today's sharper test not sure to suit so well but he remains of interest.
C&D winner last season; she had been running well in defeat prior to a lesser effort behind Thornaby Pearl three weeks ago; not discounted.
Thoroughly exposed maiden but she wasn't beaten far at Lingfield (5f, AW) when last seen eight weeks ago; has her first turf run in Britain; others look stronger for win purposes.
Running well since the visor went on in May and he has finished runner-up on his last three starts, the latest on Tuesday; should be in the thick of it again.

OwnerName: Richard Fahey Ebor Racing Club Ltd
Spotlight: Should be making a big impact off her lowly mark but her 2026 campaign has been underwhelming thus far; has won over C&D and dropping into a Class 6 will help; still not entirely convincing.
Made all to win a C&D handicap last month; in and out since but she wasn't beaten far at Ayr on Monday and this mark is unlikely to prove beyond her; one to consider.
